summary: The root ذمم primarily signifies blame, censure, or dispraise.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: َمَّهُ, (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. َمُمَ, (T, M, Msb,) inf. n. َمٌّ (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and مَ َمَّةٌ, (M, K,) He blamed, dispraised, discommended, found fault with, censured, or reprehended, him, in respect of evil conduct; ال َّمُّ signifying اللَّوْمُ (T, Mgh) فِى الإِسَآءَةِ; (T;) contr. of المَدْحُ, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) or of الحَمْدُ: (Mgh:) and, (MA,) inf. n. تَ ْمِيمٌ, (KL,) signifies the same: (MA, KL:) [or this has an intensive meaning: see its pass. part.
َمَّمَ see 1, first sentence.
فُلَانٌ يُ َامُّ عَيْشَهُ (assumed tropical:) Such a one passes his life contended with scantiness. (TA.)

ا مّ He (a man) did [or said ] that for which he should be blamed, dispraised, discommended, found fault with, censured, or reprehended; (S;) contr. of أَحْمَدَ. (A in art. حمد.) And إِلَيْهِ, (M, K,) or إِلَى النَّاسِ, (S,) He did to him, or to the people, that for which he should be blamed, &c. (S, M, K.) [Hence,] أَ َمَّتْ رَاحِلَتُهُ (tropical:) His riding-camel ceased going on; as though she made the people to blame her.

ت مّم He shunned, or avoided, (T, * Mgh,) or he preserved, or guarded, himself from, (MA,) blame, dispraise, &c.: (T, * MA, Mgh:) this is the proper meaning; and hence, (Mgh,) he felt disdain, or scorn, and shame. (S, MA, Mgh, K, KL.) One says, لَوْ لَمْ أَتْرُكِ الكَ ِبَ تَأَثُّمًا لَتَرَكْتُهُ تَ َمُّمَا [ If I did not refrain from lying for the purpose of abstaining from sin, I would refrain from it from a feeling of disdain, or scorn, or shame ].
ت امّوا They blamed, dispraised, discommended, found fault with, censured, or reprehended, one another. (M, K.)

است مّ [ He required blame, &c.; as though he called for it; or] he was blamed, or dispraised, &c. (KL.) See also 4, second sentence. And see 5, last sentence. [ است مّ بِ ِمَامِهِ is used by post-classical writers, and is perhaps a classical phrase, meaning He begged, or implored, his protection. See an instance in “ Abulfedæ Annales, ” vol. iii. p. 170.]
R. Q. 1 َمْ َمَ He made his gift small, or scanty. (IAar, T, K.)

َمٌّ inf. n. of َمَّهُ. (T, S, M, &c.) [As a simple subst., Blame, dispraise, or censure. ] And [the pl.] ُمُومٌ signifies Vices, faults, defects, or the like. (M, K. [See َامٌّ.]) See also َمِيمٌ. And see َمَّةٌ.
ِمٌّ: see َمِيمٌ. Also Excessively lean or emaciated; and perishing: (K:) or like him who is perishing. (T, TA.) See also ِمَّةٌ.

َمَّةٌ [as a subst.]; (T, Mgh;) and بِئْرٌ َمَّةٌ, (T, S, M, Mgh, K,) in which the latter word is an epithet, (Mgh,) and also, with kesr, (so in one of my copies of the S,) and, and َمِيمَةٌ; (M, K;) A well containing little water; (T, S, M, Mgh, K;) because discommended: (M, Mgh:) and, (M, K,) as some say, (M,) containing much water: thus having two contr. significations: (M, K:) pl. ِمَامٌ (T, S, M, K) and, (T, TA,) [or rather the latter is a coll. gen. n., of which َمَّةٌ is the n.

ِمَّةٌ A compact, a covenant, a contract, a league, a treaty, an engagement, a bond, or an obligation; (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) because the breaking thereof necessitates blame: (Mgh:) and a right, or due, ( حَقٌّ,) for the neglect of which one is to be blamed: (Bd in ix. 8:) [ an inviolable right or due: ] and and and signify in like manner a compact, a covenant, &c.
ِمَامٌ: see ِمَّةٌ, in three places. It is also a pl. of ِمَّةٌ [as well as syn. therewith]. (T.)

َمِيمٌ Blamed, dispraised, discommended, found fault with, censured, or reprehended; (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) i. q.; (T, M, Msb, K;) as also (T, K, TA) and, (M, K, TA,) which last is an inf. n. used as an epithet, and, like [its contr.] حَمْدٌ, is applied to a man and to a place of alighting or sojourning or abiding. (TA.) [See مُ ِمٌّ ] See also َمَّةٌ. Also, applied to water, Disliked, or disapproved. (S, K.

َمَامَةٌ: see ِمَّةٌ, in two places. Also Shame, and fear of blame: whence the saying, أَخَ َتْهُ مِنْ صَاحِبِهِ َمَامَةٌ [ Shame, and fear of blame, with respect to his companion, seized him ]: and أَصَابَتْهُ مِنْهُ َمَامَةٌ, i. e. Shame and disgrace affected him on account of him, or it.
ُمَامَةٌ (assumed tropical:) A remain, remainder, remaining portion, remnant, or relic. (K.) [See also َمَّآء, below.]
ِمَامَةٌ: see ِمَّةٌ, in two places.

بِهِ َمِيمَةٌ In him is a crippleness, or a chronic disease, (K, [in the CK َمانَةٌ is erroneously put for زَمَانَةٌ,]) or an infirmity arising therefrom or from some evil affection, (M,) that prevents him from going forth. (M, K.)

أَبْقَى َمَّآءَ الصُّبِّ (tropical:) [ He left ] the last remains [ of what was poured out, or forth, at once ]: so in the A. (TA. [But the last word is there written without any syll. signs.]) [See also ُمَامَةٌ.]
ِمِّىٌّ: see ِمَّةٌ, in the former half of the paragraph.
َمَّامٌ One who blames, dispraises, discommends, &c., much, or often. (TA.)
َامٌّ and َامٌ, with and without teshdeed, [the latter belonging to art. يم,] A vice, fault, defect, or the like. (As, T.) [See also َمٌّ.]
أَ َمُّ A horse fatigued, and standing still. (TA.)
مَ َمٌّ and مَ ِمٌّ: see ِمَّةٌ, in the latter part of the paragraph.

مُ ِّمٌّ A thing blamed, dispraised, &c.; [like َمِيمٌ;] or made, or caused, to be faulty, or defective, or to have a vice, fault, defect, or the like; (S. K;) as also. (K.) And A man (S) in whom is no motion. (S, K.)
مِ َمٌّ: see the next preceding paragraph.

مَ َمَّةٌ, with fet-h only [to the, A cause of blame, dispraise, discommendation, censure, or reprehension; a blamable, or discommendable, quality or action; ] a thing for which one is, or is to be, blamed, dispraised, discommended, found fault with, censured, or reprehended: contr. of مَحْمَدَةٌ: (S:) [pl. مَ َامٌّ.] You say, البُخْلُ مَ َمَّةٌ, (S, K,) i. e. [ Niggardliness is ] one of the things for which one is, or is to be, blamed, &c.
مَ ِمَّةٌ: see ِمَّةٌ, in six places. And see also َمَامَةٌ.
مُ َمَّمٌ A man blamed, dispraised, discommended, found fault with, censured, or reprehended, much. (S, K.) And A place held in reverence, respect, or honour. (TA.)
مَ ْمُومٌ: see َمِيمٌ, first sentence.
مُسْتَ َمٌّ: see 5, last sentence.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
